name: Captain Feed for YouTube
author: Dipak Dodiya

sections.description:
Captain Feed for YouTube is a powerful yet easy-to-use WordPress plugin that lets you display stunning YouTube content on your website with full control over layout, styling, and behavior.

Whether you want to showcase your YouTube channel, a playlist, YouTube Shorts, or hand-picked individual videos — this plugin makes it simple. No coding required.

Designed for performance and flexibility, it integrates smoothly with Elementor and works with any modern WordPress theme.

Perfect for creators, businesses, and marketers who want to grow their YouTube presence directly from their website.

Key Features

  • 📺 Display YouTube Channel Feeds
  • 📋 Show Full Playlist Videos
  • 🩳 YouTube Shorts vertical feed support (NEW in 1.0.1)
  • 🎬 Embed Single or Multiple Hand-picked Videos
  • 🔍 YouTube Search-based Video Feed
  • 🎨 Multiple display layouts (Grid, List, Cards, Carousel)
  • ⚡ Lightning-fast with built-in API response caching
  • 📱 Fully responsive and mobile-friendly
  • 🔌 Elementor widget integration
  • 🔁 Plugin Rollback to any previous version (NEW in 1.0.1)
  • 📖 Built-in Documentation pages (NEW in 1.0.1)
  • 🧩 No coding required

Supported Feed Types

  • YouTube Channel Feed — Display all recent videos from any channel
  • YouTube Playlist Feed — Show videos from any public playlist
  • YouTube Shorts Feed — Display vertical short-form videos in a 9:16 grid
  • Individual Video Feed — Curate and embed specific videos
  • YouTube Search Feed — Show videos matching any search query

Usage

After activation:

  1. Get a YouTube API Key — Create a free API key from Google Cloud Console. See the built-in Documentation page for a step-by-step guide.
  2. Create a Feed — Choose your feed type: Channel, Playlist, Shorts, Search, or Single Videos.
  3. Enter your Source — Add your Channel ID, @handle, Playlist ID, or Video URLs.
  4. Customize — Select layout style, number of videos, and display options.
  5. Publish — Use the shortcode [captain-feed-for-youtube id="X"] on any page.

Getting Your YouTube IDs

Use the built-in Documentation section inside the plugin admin for detailed guides on:

  • How to create a Google YouTube API Token
  • How to find a Channel ID or Nickname
  • How to use YouTube Channel @Handles
  • How to find a Playlist ID

External Services

This plugin connects to the YouTube Data API v3 provided by Google to fetch YouTube channel information, playlists, Shorts, and videos for display on your website.

What data is sent and when:

  • YouTube API Key (required to authenticate requests)
  • YouTube Channel ID or @Handle (to fetch channel videos)
  • Playlist ID (to fetch playlist videos)
  • Video ID(s) (to fetch specific video details)
  • Search query term (for search-based feeds)

This data is sent to Google’s servers only when:
– A feed is loaded on the frontend
– A feed is previewed in the admin dashboard
– Cached feed data expires and is refreshed

No visitor personal data is collected or transmitted by this plugin.

Service Provider: Google LLC
YouTube Data API Terms of Service: https://developers.google.com/youtube/terms/api-services-terms-of-service
Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/captain-feed-for-youtube directory, or install directly through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin from the Plugins screen.
  3. Go to Captain Feed for YouTube in the WordPress admin menu.
  4. Click Create Feeds and choose your feed type (Channel, Playlist, Shorts, Search, or Single Videos).
  5. Enter your YouTube API Key and the relevant Channel ID, Playlist ID, or search term.
  6. Customize the layout and click Save.
  7. Copy the generated shortcode and paste it on any page, post, or widget area.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require Elementor?

No, Elementor is completely optional. The plugin works with any theme using shortcodes. Elementor support is included for users who want drag-and-drop control.

How do I get a YouTube API Key?

Go to the Documentation section inside the plugin admin for a full step-by-step guide. It’s free and takes about 5 minutes.

Can I display YouTube Shorts?

Yes! Version 1.0.1 adds a dedicated YouTube Shorts feed type that displays short-form vertical videos in a beautiful 9:16 grid layout — similar to TikTok or Instagram Reels.

Can I show playlist videos?

Yes, simply enter your Playlist ID when creating a Playlist feed. The plugin will automatically fetch and display all videos from that playlist.

Can I display my entire channel feed?

Yes, enter your Channel ID or @handle. The plugin supports both formats.

Can I display videos from multiple channels or playlists?

Yes, create a separate feed for each channel or playlist, then place the shortcodes anywhere on your site.

What is the Rollback feature?

The Rollback feature (added in v1.0.1) lets you safely downgrade the plugin to any of the last 10 previous versions directly from the admin panel — without needing FTP or manual file uploads.

Is my visitors’ data shared with YouTube/Google?

No visitor personal data is collected or transmitted. Only public YouTube content identifiers (channel IDs, playlist IDs, etc.) are sent to the YouTube API to fetch video data.

Is it beginner-friendly?

Absolutely! Everything is visual and easy to configure. No coding knowledge is required.

Does the plugin cache API responses?

Yes. The plugin uses WordPress transients to cache YouTube API responses, reducing API quota usage and improving frontend performance.

What happens when I uninstall the plugin?

The plugin includes a clean uninstall routine. You can optionally clear all stored feeds, settings, and cached data when uninstalling.
